source.title: The central nucleus of the amygdala and the construction of defensive modes across the threat-imminence continuum

confidence_rationale: Review proposing that CeA's mutually inhibitory circuits select among defensive modes by threat imminence, executing defensive behaviours to PREVIOUSLY FORMED threat associations. Supports MECH-599's consumer contract: defensive mode selection is driven by learned threat predictions (and their imminence), not by accumulated injury. Already recorded for MECH-489 (2026-08-15 entry); this entry records the MECH-599-specific mapping.
failure_signatures: Defensive modes are selected against learned threat associations organised by imminence; a defensive consumer that reads only accumulated injury has no imminence variable and cannot reproduce the mode ordering.

mapping.source_claim_statement: CeA's mutually inhibitory circuits use a winner-takes-all strategy to transition across defensive modes and execute specific defensive behaviours to previously formed threat associations, organised along a threat-imminence continuum.
mapping.ree_translation: For MECH-599 the point is the input to the consumer: CeA builds defensive modes from previously formed threat associations and their imminence -- i.e. from a threat predictor's output. That is the MECH-599 consumer contract (SD-099 release, MECH-279 freeze entry and E3 harm scoring should read predicted threat). Imminence is a variable REE lacks; a cue-specific predictor is a prerequisite for it.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Review/perspective. Imminence has no REE analogue; the mapping is to the input type of the consumer, not to mode selection itself. See the MECH-489 entry for the selection-architecture mapping.
mapping.source_context: Review of rodent defensive-behaviour paradigms and CeA circuitry

confidence_components.notes: Separate entry from the MECH-489 one because the mapping is different; same source.
